title: A pond
summary: Throw stones in a random pond. Only teach the person reading the ripples.

cards.text:
A crowd of buckets, wired at random, ripples when input arrives.
You do not teach the crowd.

You teach a simple reader on top.
Different stones should leave different ripples.

question.why: The pond stays random. The reader learns.
question.simpler: If two stones leave the same ripple, the reader cannot help.

question.prompt: A pond that settles to the same pattern for every input is doing the job.
question.why: That erases the difference you needed.
question.simpler: The title of the paper is computing without those stable wipe-outs.

recall.question: In a liquid state machine, which part is trained?
recall.answer: The readout. The pond stays random.

deeper.note: Maass, Natschläger, and Markram named the two hopes: separation, and a reader that can approximate the functions you care about.

paper.title: Real-time computing without stable states: a new framework for neural computation based on perturbations

terms.plain: a random pool plus a trained reader
terms.definition: A reservoir of spiking neurons that is not trained. Only a readout on its state is trained.
